newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman approves oil deal with Saudi firm.
newsitem.headline: Oman approves oil deal with Saudi firm.

text.p: Oman on Saturday approved a $50.5 million oil exploration deal the Gulf Arab state signed in January with Nimir Petroleum Company Ltd. of Saudi Arabia, the official news agency ONA said.
Oman's head of state, Sultan Qaboos bin Said, issued a decree approving the concession covering an area of 15,000 square km (5,790 sq miles) in bloc three in northeast Oman, the agency said.

The Saudi company will conduct geophysical and geological studies in the first phase of the project before agreeing with the oil ministry on a location to drill two deep wells to look for oil and gas.
Oman produces 900,000 barrels per day of oil -- which accounts for nearly three-quarters of government revenue.
